findings.reason: At base 6aca82f, TV items 2 and 26 remain in SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality, whose cover list promises the algebraic Tate construction and character extension. Feng items 65, 66 and 68 and its first route explicitly assign the Tate diagonal, unique extension and Frobenius linearization to SheafTheoreticSmithTheory, naming TV as a consumer. These are inconsistent ownership instructions, not merely two citations of one theorem. The underlying tensor-with-Frobenius construction must support modules as well as algebras; the vector-space version should not be lost when reconciling the two. Accept the repair as an explicit supplier/import boundary and removal of the second construction promise, preserving TV's topological Smith applications. A proposed roadmap is not an implemented declaration or an existing atlas stage: do not change these items to library or invent a planned stage identifier before that owner is integrated. Retain the items as traceable source uses with exactly one construction owner.

EllipticCurves Layer 5 explicitly owns the continuous nonabelian H1 prerequisite, and the Layer 7 dependency note spells out cocycles, coboundary equivalence, pointed H1, functoriality and restriction for profinite groups acting on discrete groups. A finite cyclic group with its discrete topology is profinite, and every action on a discrete group is continuous, so TV item 3 is a specialization of that plan. Mathlib's pinned CategoryTheory/Sites/NonabelianCohomology/H1.lean instead defines H1 for a presheaf of groups and a family of objects; it does not discharge this group-action statement. Cite tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-5-twists-aec-x2-x5, leaving the cyclic-generator cocycle formula and its comparison as an explicit adapter. Items 4 and 5 need their own exact-sequence and prime-to-p arguments. The fact that Layer 5 labels its classification a stretch milestone does not authorize a second foundational H1 construction in the TV route. Request the prerequisite from that owner if necessary.

Published pp. 198 and 212 explicitly invoke three inputs absent as separate extraction items: connected finite-field H1 vanishing, closedness of the finite-order automorphism's conjugacy class in characteristic zero, and a sigma-stable Borel/torus pair containing the selected regular semisimple element of H. PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18/lang-theorem already routes Lang's theorem to RG2.3; use that owner, while distinguishing its source-route request from the current atlas paragraph, which does not yet state Lang's theorem. Correct the proposed Borel statement: finite order over an arbitrary algebraically closed field is insufficient. In characteristic p, conjugation by a nonidentity unipotent element of SL2 of order p cannot stabilize a Borel and a maximal torus within it: that element would belong to N(B) intersect N(T) = T, a contradiction. Keep the characteristic-zero, connected-reductive G, connected H = G^sigma setting of TV, and x regular semisimple in H, not an invented regularity hypothesis in G. Reeder Lemma 3.2's proof independently invokes semisimplicity and a stable Borel/torus; it is not an arbitrary-characteristic finite-order theorem. Joyner Corollary 5.8, read on p. 279 with the semidirect-product setup on p. 270, supplies closedness for semisimple twisted classes. Keep the characteristic-zero/semisimple hypotheses and any reduction needed to apply its setup. Add these supplier statements and prerequisite edges, preserving E27's exclusion of bad special fibres, instead of treating their citations as proofs of the consuming propositions.

Item 16's single library status covers both the Hecke algebra and general right modules V^K and k[X/K]. The cited pinned declarations construct the double-coset carrier, convolution ring and anti-involution data, not those general actions. I read Mathlib Defs.lean:75,183,189 and Tau Ceti Associativity.lean:485 and Commutativity.lean:98,478 at the protocol pins. The extra library case is real: LeftCosetModule.Basic:296,314 and Action:383 construct the opposite-Hecke-ring module on the free module of left cosets, corresponding to X = G. They do not quantify over arbitrary X or V. Split the library algebra/special module from the general action and comparison obligations, retaining the corrected coset convention already in the item and the warning that k[X/K] need not equal k[X]^K. Amend the proposed routing repair: current SR.1 expressly plans integral double-coset operators by finite correspondences where averaging is unavailable. Thus its scope is not limited to invertible-denominator idempotent corners, as the old review note says. Reconcile the general module construction with SR.1 and leave TV-specific comparisons/applications here; do not establish a second foundational Hecke action solely because the coefficient characteristic is p.

Read the full cited stage descriptions and the four item statements. AA.0 builds restricted products of groups and measures; AA.4 builds approximation and level maps. Neither states item 37's restricted tensor product isomorphism for Hecke algebras. AA.3 supplies reduction theory but does not state item 43's properness theorem for H(F)\H(A) -> G(F)\G(A). ALS.3 constructs correspondence actions, but item 18's particular singular-chain action still needs a comparison with them. For item 38, AA.1 spreading out, RG2.3 integral-model/reduction inputs and SR.4 Satake contribute distinct parts; the current citations do not isolate them. Correct the statuses or split supported inputs from the missing comparison/theorem and route each remaining obligation. Refine the red-team fix under single ownership: AF.0 already owns restricted tensor products of adelic test functions, SR.1 the general Hecke algebra, AA.3 arithmetic quotient geometry and ALS.3 chain-level Hecke correspondences. Request the missing algebra-isomorphism, properness and comparison statements from those owners as appropriate, then import them into SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality. Mere relevance of a stage, or an unfulfilled note saying to split an item, cannot justify planned status for the whole statement.

Published Section 5.5 on p. 197 assumes connected reductive G and connected fixed group H. Theorem 5.8 uses those data without adding semisimplicity. The route-1 final theorem instead says semisimple G, excluding the GL_a x GL_b inside GL_n example of Section 9.5 and reductive cyclic base change in Section 9.4. Replace that condition by connected reductive G and retain the sigma-stable level, fixed-level, compatible archimedean compact and sufficiently-small-level conditions of Section 5.5. An additional edit is essential: the brief's Theorem 6.5 currently inherits 'the same data'. Once 5.8 is widened, state semisimple G explicitly for 6.5. The published 6.5 on p. 203 adds that hypothesis and also requires S disjoint from V and the places above p. The correction must not silently widen the linkage theorem.

Verified the printed page images of Sections 7.4(b) and 9.3, the Section 2.9 parameter convention, and preprint Section 7.5, pp. 27-28. Section 7.4(b) requires psi^2 = delta = |Sigma_G|_v. The norm-on-prime-ideals character specified in 9.3(b) has local value q_v on a uniformizer, so its pullback by Sigma_G/2 squares to delta^{-1}. For split SL2, p = 7, v over 3 and t = diag(3,1/3), delta(t) = 3^{-2} = 4 in F_7, whereas the stated character squares to 3^2 = 2. This is an actual failure and is not repaired by E32's changes to the dual-torus normalization alone. Invert the prime-to-p ideal character in item 59 and record a separate, version-collated source issue. With reciprocity sending a uniformizer to arithmetic Frobenius, define the corrected global character as cyclo^{-1} composed with reciprocity and then with Sigma_G/2. Its unramified local components away from p are |.|_v modulo p; the inverse pseudoroot has parameter (Sigma_G^*/2)(cyclo(Frob_v)), so published (9.3.1) can remain. Do not literally reduce the real-valued global idelic norm modulo p: its p-adic local factors cannot be mapped that way to k^*, and the character at primes above p must be supplied by reciprocity. State the Frobenius convention. The proposed blanket 'affects nothing' is too weak for the false general assertion that the stated character is a pseudoroot; record that stated construction as affected, while distinguishing downstream examples for which inversion agrees. This does not show failure for every prime p >= 7 or every place.

All three named pairs restate both the local sigma-dual construction and its global consequence, rather than giving a supplier and a referencing consumer. The Sp pair also has incompatible ranges: rev-exotic-mod-2-transfer-from permits n = 1 while rev-exotic-transfer-from-sp-2n correctly excludes it. For g = [[a,b],[c,d]] of determinant one and J = [[0,1],[-1,0]], direct multiplication gives J(g^T)^{-1}J^{-1} = g, so sigma is the identity on SL2, not an automorphism of order two. Require n >= 2. Keep each Section 9 construction once and have the corresponding introduction/global-transfer item invoke it together with 5.8 and 9.1. Preserve the global conclusions and all their hypotheses; in the Eisenstein case retain the inverse-Frobenius twist which removes the Frobenius from the block inclusion, and in the G2 case retain the semidirect-product/Galois action. A local construction and its global consequence are distinct obligations even after their duplicate construction text is removed.

Published Proposition 5.4, p. 197, and preprint p. 16 both state only K'_v subset K_v, but immediately use the finite group K/K' and its Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence. Without normality that quotient is not a group, so the displayed proof does not establish the full statement. Add the normal-level hypothesis to the extracted proved version and record the general statement as having an unfilled proof gap, rather than claiming a counterexample to the proposition. Normal small levels suffice for the later reduction when V omits a finite place: take a sufficiently small open normal subgroup there (and a sigma-stable normal refinement when needed), leaving the prescribed places unchanged. Keep the source's orbifold/equivariant interpretation at nonfree levels. Passing to a normal core proves occurrence at that finer level but does not by itself descend the eigensystem to an arbitrary intermediate K', so it is not a proof of the original unrestricted assertion. Record the issue against both versions and scope its downstream effect to the argument actually used.

The citation on published p. 205 points to [34, p. 173], but the bibliography on p. 228 identifies [34] as Regular elements of semisimple algebraic groups, pp. 49-80. Preprint pp. 23 and 48 repeat the incompatible references [31, p. 173/177]. I went beyond the red team's conjectured replacement and read the original Yale Lectures on Chevalley Groups scan, Section 11, printed pp. 172-174 and 177 (PDF pp. 179-181,184). Theorem 32 and proof step (3), p. 173, construct the orbit-longest-element reflection; step (5), p. 174, proves that these generate the fixed Weyl group. The corollary on p. 177 gives the root-equivalence classes, including A1^n and A2 in the length-preserving diagram-automorphism case used by TV. Its general statement also lists C2 and G2 for the other allowed transformations; do not omit that scope when citing it. Thus add the bibliographic source issue and replace the references with verified locators in the Yale notes, rather than leaving 'to be confirmed' or asserting an unverified page. Preserve [34] for the other, genuinely different results that TV cites from it.

Likewise the canonical torus over O and its descent must retain FKP's actual group-scheme hypotheses. The red team's proposed route-2 owner is a possible coordination proposal, not a reason to bypass PROTOCOL Section 15's most-foundational-owner test or to delete the separate C-group deformation theorem.
